title: The per-rank byte floor
caption: Reducing N contributions and returning the result needs at least 2(N-1) item transfers in aggregate: N-1 to combine, N-1 to distribute. A balanced schedule gives every rank the average share, so the per-rank sent volume approaches 2M as N grows. This is the floor every AllReduce schedule is judged against.

symbols.meaning: rank count in the process group
tensor bytes per rank (e.g. 1 GB buffer, 140 GB 70B gradient)
per-link bandwidth (50 GB/s NDR in the reference model)

title: Ring AllReduce cost
caption: The ring hits the byte floor and pays for it with rounds: 2(N-1) steps of M/N chunks, each charged one startup alpha. On the chapter's 64-GPU, 1 GB, 50 GB/s case the byte term is ~39.4 ms against a simple tree's ~240 ms, but the latency column grows linearly with N.

symbols.meaning: per-message startup cost (effective ~1-3 us on NDR)
round count: N-1 scatter-reduce steps + N-1 all-gather steps
per-round chunk size; the regime each step sits in is set by the chunk, not the tensor

title: The ring-tree crossover
caption: Ring's excess startup (~N alpha) balances tree's excess byte time (~log2 N x M/beta) at this message size. At 256 GPUs on a 200 Gbps fabric with alpha = 1 us the crossover sits near 1 MB: tree schedules win small collectives, ring wins large ones. The boundary moves with group size and fabric.

symbols.meaning: payload at which the two schedule families break even
n*, the fabric's latency-bandwidth crossover (~75 KB on NDR, >500 KB on NVLink)
tree depth; rounds the tree saves relative to the ring's 2(N-1)

title: Three-phase hierarchical cost
caption: Exploits the bandwidth cliff instead of paying it: reduce inside each node over fast NVLink, ring per-shard across the slow inter-node ports in parallel, broadcast the shard result back inside the node. On 128 nodes x 8 GPUs with a 350 GB gradient the modeled gain is ~4-5x over the flat bound; the inter-node phase alone runs ~4.4 ms.

symbols.meaning: intra-node reduce at NVLink rates (~450 GB/s/direction)
inter-node ring over independent NDR ports, payload per port cut 8x
intra-node broadcast of the reduced shard

title: What overlap can hide
caption: LogP separates network transit (L, overlappable beneath independent computation) from processor overhead (o per side, never overlappable because it occupies the execution resource). In the worked toy: 100 us of L hides under 500 us of compute, but 100 us of 2o stays exposed, giving 600 us effective. This is why kernel-bypass and GPUDirect matter more to hiding than raw link bandwidth.

symbols.meaning: network latency; time data is in flight while the processor works
per-side processor overhead: dispatch, kernel launch, memory registration, runtime progress
independent computation available to overlap (the next layer's backward)

title: The residual accumulator
caption: The correction that turns a biased compressor into a convergent method: add the residual to the new gradient, compress and transmit the corrected vector, keep the untransmitted difference. In the book's trace the naive run transmits 0 of a true 1.6 while error feedback transmits 2 and holds -0.4 in residual. A finite run ends with residual still untransmitted, but the telescope prevents systematic loss.

symbols.meaning: residual: compression error carried from prior steps
